Pregnancy. Insulin is generally preferred for treatment of dia- betes during pregnancy. However, there are limited data to sug- gest that metformin does not increase the risk of congenital abnormalities1,2 and does not adversely affect pregnancy out- come in diabetic women.2 A controlled study comparing insulin with metformin in gestational diabetes is underway.3 The use of metformin to improve ovulation in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is increasing. There is growing evidence to suggest that metformin used before and during pregnancy in these women does not increase the risk of congenital abnormali- ties,1,4-6 and may reduce first trimester spontaneous abortion,4,6 which is common in women with PCOS. 1.
